newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police kill six gunmen after they surrender.
newsitem.headline: Thai police kill six gunmen after they surrender.

text.p: Thai police shot dead six gunmen on Wednesday after they surrendered and released three hostages held overnight, police and witnesses said.
Police said they were forced to shoot the suspected drug traffickers, who were in handcuffs after surrendering to police and releasing the hostages, because they had tried to fight back.

Police arrested the six men, escorted them out of the house they had commandeered and were wading through floodwaters towards the police station when the officers decided to go back to search for more evidence, witnesses and police said.
"Then after about 30 minutes we heard gunfire and the police came out and said the suspects were shot because they resisted," one witness said.
The men, armed with automatic rifles, apparently comandeered the house and took a man, woman and boy hostage after being chased by police at around 5 p.m. (1000 gmt) on Tuesday.
Several hundred police surrounded the house but did not raid it because they feared the hostages would be shot, police said.
At around mid-morning on Wednesday, a police officer went inside the house and negotiated the release of the hostages and the gunmen's surrender, police said.
